ops.title: fusekit v0.30.0 + cc-pool v0.40.0: the orphaned-go-nfsv4 recovery — a crashed holder's servers answered EPERM on every mount and no successor could reap them; now carcass-detected, cross-generation reaped (kill-time re-confirmed), and doctor-reported
ops.body:
The 2026-07-03 incident root fix. A fusekit mount-holder that dies without an exit path (SIGTRAP
inside libc `exit()` after a clean "mountd stopped" — an ObjC/fuse-t bg thread racing Go runtime
teardown) leaves its spawned **go-nfsv4 servers orphaned**, still bound to their sockets and
answering **EPERM on every op**. Four detectors all misread EPERM as healthy, and the reaper was
direct-children-only, so no successor holder could reap the previous generation's orphans → new
sessions saw a broken config view. See [[holder-bg-band-incident]].

**Fix — fusekit v0.30.0** (all darwin, `!darwin` no-ops):
- carcass verdict: EPERM/EACCES join ENOTCONN/EIO/hang as carcass signatures (statAnswers).
- `ReapOrphanedServers(roots []string) []int`: scans kern.proc.all for comm==go-nfsv4 whose
  argv mountpoint is under a root; SIGKILLs only after a carcass stat. **Every kill is
  re-confirmed at signal time** with `reconfirmOrphan`/`pidStillServes`: FRESH per-candidate
  carcass stat (NOT memoized across the loop — a mount going live mid-sweep must not be judged
  on a stale verdict) + argv-mountpoint re-read (comm is identical across ALL go-nfsv4, so a
  reused PID on a DIFFERENT path is only caught by the mountpoint check). The direct-child and
  per-dir (ClearCarcass forceReap) paths carry the same PID-reuse guard. The reconfirm→kill
  window is irreducible on macOS (no pidfd) — accepted.
- `ErrProbeDenied`/`ErrProbeMissing` + `ProbeOpenVerdict(err)`: EPERM/EACCES wedge-probe = dead
  verdict, not the "probe missing = old holder" no-verdict fold.
- ship-gated `FUSEKIT_HOLDER_KILL_GROUP=1` setpgid isolation (default OFF pending VM 10-kill-cycle
  gate); log-fd O_CLOEXEC + stdio→/dev/null so children don't inherit the holder log.
- `scripts/vm/scenarios/repro-holder-crash-orphan.sh` (authored; run gates seam-5).

**Fix — cc-pool v0.40.0** (consumes v0.30.0): probe.go maps ErrProbeDenied→ErrProbeWedged
(strike+remount). Daemon reaps on holder death via `ReapOrphanedServers([MuxRootDir, AccountsDir])`
— roots MUST include the mux root (under mux the orphan's argv mountpoint IS ~/.cc-pool/mnt, not
the account dir) — then the idle-gated force-unmount. The crash memory (`servedMounts`) survives a
healthy→degraded→unreachable slide (markDegraded latches it; noteUnmounted only disarms while
HEALTHY — an empty map during degraded is a wiped cache, not a drain) AND a cold start reaps at
reconcileOverlays. **Live sessions still gate every force-unmount** (never force-unmount under a
session — kernel-panic class); the reap frees the orphan underneath regardless. Doctor reports
"holder dead, N orphaned mount(s)" with blocking session PIDs.

Method note: 3 codex review rounds (finder+refuter) caught 2 real criticals the first author
missed — markDegraded swallowing the transition, and PID-reuse killing a fresh server on a
different path via the comm-only check. Adversarial refute earns its keep on kill logic.
Fleet is on File Provider now ([[fp-backend-rollout]]); the fuse path stays supported and this
makes it recoverable. Related: [[claude-pool-project]], [[fusekit-proc-extraction]].
